memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They answered Joshua, "Your servants were clearly told how the Lord your God had commanded his servant Moses to give you the whole land and to wipe out all its inhabitants from before you. So we feared for our lives because of you, and that is why we did this. We are now in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you." — Josh 9:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now, finally, the Gibeonites tell the truth. Confronted by Joshua, they confess their real motive: "we feared for our lives because of you, and that is why we did this." No more disguises, no more elaborate story. They lay themselves bare and place themselves entirely at Israel's mercy: "We are now in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you."

There is something moving in this complete surrender. Having been exposed, they do not argue, make excuses, or try another scheme. They simply throw themselves on the mercy of Israel and Israel's God. It is a picture of humble submission — coming to the end of all self-protection and casting oneself entirely upon another's mercy.

And notice what drove their whole scheme in the first place: they had heard of God's power and commands, and they wanted to live. Beneath all their deception was a genuine recognition that Israel's God was real and not to be resisted. Their methods were wrong, but their instinct to seek refuge with God's people was, in the end, the thing that saved them.

This surrender is a pale but real picture of how we come to God. We, too, come to the end of our schemes and self-protection and cast ourselves wholly on His mercy, saying in effect, "I am now in Your hands." And the wonder of the gospel is that when we place ourselves at God's mercy through Christ, we do not find condemnation but grace. "Whoever comes to me I will never drive away," Jesus promised (John 6:37). The One into whose hands we fall is full of mercy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you come to the end of your self-protection and cast yourself on God's mercy?
2. Why is honest surrender so much better than continued scheming?
3. How does Jesus' promise never to turn away those who come to Him encourage you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I place myself entirely in Your hands. I let go of my schemes and self-protection and cast myself on Your mercy, trusting that in Christ You receive me with grace. Amen.
